lines.caption: This is a tour of pull request 87, which keeps a pull request session's context small, so it costs less.
It has three parts: what the PR adds, how it was checked, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
A new Context section in CLAUDE.md, a new build-verify agent, and quieter log reading in two skills.
First, a noisy command writes everything to a log file and echoes only its exit code.
The session reads that exit code first, to see whether the command passed.
Then it reads the last 30 lines, or on a failure, the lines its skill's grep picks out.
lines.say: Then it reads the last thirty lines, or on a failure, the lines its skill's grep picks out.

lines.caption: So the context holds the exit code and a few lines, never the whole log.
Second, heavy steps move into subagents, starting with the new build-verify agent, which builds and runs the tests.
The local review of the diff runs in a fresh agent that returns only its findings.
The explainer page and its narration are written by a subagent too.
Each sends back a short answer, with any failing lines copied exactly, not paraphrased.
Third, reads stay narrow: grep for a function, then read only its lines.
And the main session never opens a screenshot; subagents read those instead.
Every turn re-reads the whole context, and one batch session reached about 567k tokens and cost about $33.6.
lines.say: Every turn re-reads the whole context, and one batch session reached about five hundred sixty-seven thousand tokens, and cost about thirty-three dollars sixty.

lines.caption: The batch skill's brief now points every group's session to these rules.
A redirect keeps a command's exit code, while a pipe into tail hides it, so logs go to a file first.
Build, test, render and narration commands all log to a file, and the exit code is always read first.
On a failure, each skill or agent names its own grep, so only the failing lines come back.
build-verify always builds, installs and tests in one go, so the tests run against the build it just made.
The review agent and the explainer subagent work the same way, and this page was written by one.
Their fixed short answers keep confident wording from hiding a real failure.
Reads use grep first, then a slice of the file, and screenshots stay with the subagents.
In the grep table, build-verify holds the only test pattern, which keeps every result and each failure's details.
The build pattern finds compiler, linker and Python errors, then the whole traceback when there is one.
And the narration check's pattern keeps every stale line and the verdict.
build-verify always answers in this fixed shape, ending with the exact failing lines.
Outside a cloud container it only builds, and in one it always installs and tests the build it just made.
The PR changes CLAUDE.md, three skills and the CI test script, adds the agent, plus this page and its narration.
To undo it, revert the PR, and sessions go back to printing output inline.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
It follows the pr-digest agent, the screenshot auditors, and the test script's own result lines.
Before CI's review, the building session grepped a 9-line sample log, and visual-verify's first pattern kept 7 lines.
lines.say: Before C I's review, the building session grepped a nine-line sample log, and visual-verify's first pattern kept seven lines.

lines.caption: build-verify's pattern kept all 9 lines of the same log.
lines.say: build-verify's pattern kept all nine lines of the same log.

lines.caption: A redirect kept the failing exit code of 1, while a pipe into tail showed 0.
lines.say: A redirect kept the failing exit code of one, while a pipe into tail showed zero.

lines.caption: It also checked that the untracked-files list leaves out the debian folder.
The Thunar build and the new agent itself were not run: no code changed, and agents load at session start.
CI's first run needed no screenshot audit, and its explainer job found the narration current.
After the last fix, the test script still parses, and CI's build and verify on that push haven't run yet.
A fresh review agent found 7 problems, 2 of them high, and all 7 were fixed.
lines.say: A fresh review agent found seven problems, two of them high, and all seven were fixed.

lines.caption: Several greps matched the wrong lines, so now each skill or agent gives its own, and no stale line is dropped.
build-verify could have installed on the owner's machine, and now it installs only in a cloud container.
Smaller gaps were closed, and the explainer's render check now always runs in its subagent.
CI's own review then found 8 more, 1 medium and 7 low, all confirmed, and all 8 got a fix in one push.
lines.say: C I's own review then found eight more, one medium and seven low, all confirmed, and all eight got a fix in one push.

lines.caption: The medium one: the quiet narration check wrote to a log path nothing had set, so it would always fail.
The cloud guard first covered only install, while CLAUDE.md promised it for the tests too.
The explainer subagent now does the work itself, and a later page fix renders the page again.
The build grep now catches linker and Python errors, and the warnings filter counts new files.
And there is now one verify path and one grep, with visual-verify's capture going through build-verify.
CI's second review resolved 3, kept 5 open, and found 4 more lows, all now fixed for its next review to check.
lines.say: C I's second review resolved three, kept five open, and found four more lows, all now fixed for its next review to check.

lines.caption: The tests then ran only when the installed version matched, which the third review found too weak.
build-verify holds the only copy of the run grep, which now keeps warnings too, and visual-verify refers to it.
The explainer subagent never hands the work on, and narration step 4 renders the page again first.
The untracked-files list no longer picks up the build's staging folders under debian.
And the make-video log now follows the temp folder setting instead of a fixed path.
CI's third review resolved 4 more, kept 2 open, and found 7 new ones, 1 of them medium.
lines.say: C I's third review resolved four more, kept two open, and found seven new ones, one of them medium.

lines.caption: The guard then compared the installed binary, which the fourth review found too narrow.
visual-verify stopped repeating that check, and the fourth round removed the guard altogether.
A failed build then returned the log's last 30 lines, which could still lose a traceback's top frames.
lines.say: A failed build then returned the log's last thirty lines, which could still lose a traceback's top frames.

lines.caption: Smaller gaps: a run warnings line in the output, the temp folder setting for the render, and clearer step wording.
One low finding was accepted: files under debian are never compiled, so the warnings filter loses nothing.
CI's fourth review resolved 5 more and found 8 new ones, 2 of them medium.
lines.say: C I's fourth review resolved five more and found eight new ones, two of them medium.

lines.caption: A stale data package or library could slip past the guard, so build-verify now always builds, installs and tests together.
A failed build now returns the traceback itself, wherever it sits in the log.
Smaller gaps: the render snippet works across shell calls, and warnings appear only once.
Two lows were accepted: a small overlap in the build output is needed, and one wording is already accurate.
CI's fifth review resolved 3 more and found 5 new ones, 2 of them medium.
lines.say: C I's fifth review resolved three more and found five new ones, two of them medium.

lines.caption: Apt skips a deb whose version is already installed, so build-verify's install step then ended with dpkg, which always unpacks.
With a capture run, visual-verify now checks for the manifest only after the capture writes it.
The run argument and the README now say it builds, installs and captures, in a cloud container only.
Two lows were accepted: 40 lines cover the build's short tracebacks, and a fresh build is what proves the branch.
lines.say: Two lows were accepted: forty lines cover the build's short tracebacks, and a fresh build is what proves the branch.

lines.caption: CI's sixth review passed, resolved 3 more, and found 5 plausible ones, and the owner chose to fix the medium one here.
lines.say: C I's sixth review passed, resolved three more, and found five plausible ones, and the owner chose to fix the medium one here.

lines.caption: The CI install script now reinstalls the built debs itself, which also fixes three of the lows.
The last low was accepted, since those early checks can only fail inconclusive, never pass wrongly.
That makes 37 findings over six reviews: six accepted, and the rest fixed or resolved.
lines.say: That makes thirty-seven findings over six reviews: six accepted, and the rest fixed or resolved.

lines.caption: The build-verify agent first runs in the next pull request session, after the merge.
The real test is the next batch group's context and cost, against 567k tokens and $33.6 for #82.
lines.say: The real test is the next batch group's context and cost, against five hundred sixty-seven thousand tokens and thirty-three dollars sixty for number 82.

lines.caption: On the pull request, the summary comment shows build and verify running their steps on the push that changes the CI script.
The CI runs are linked too: the first run with all its jobs, and the five later reviews.
Part 3. What comes later.
No issue builds on this one, and the next batch group is the first to measure it.
If sessions still near compaction, splitting each group into an implementing and a review session may follow.
In short: logs stay in files, heavy work goes to subagents, and sessions read only what they need.
